      UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This petition seeks Special Leave to Appeal against the
impugned judgment and order dated 04.05.2026 passed by
the Single Bench of the High Court of Judicature for
Rajasthan at Jaipur in S.B. Criminal Misc. Suspension of
Sentence Application No. 2222/2025 in Criminal Appeal No.
2916/2025,  whereby  the  High  Court  rejected  the
petitioners’  application  for  suspension  of  sentence
during the pendency of their appeal.
2. By  judgment  dated  17.09.2025  passed  by  the  learned
Special Judge, POCSO Act Cases, Jhunjhunu, Petitioner No.
1 (Ashish Kumar) was convicted under Sections 363, 366A,
and 376 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), Sections 3 & 4 of
the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO)
Act, and Sections 3(2)(v) & 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act. Petitioner No. 2 (Naveen Kumar) was convicted under
Sections 363, 366A, and 376 IPC, as well as Sections 3 &
4 of the POCSO Act. Both petitioners were sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty (20) years along
with fine.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that The
petitioners have served about 1½  years of incarceration
and had no prior antecedents. Additionally, the High
Court previously granted bail on 11.12.2024 considering
SLP(Crl.)  No.12819/2026                                             2

--- Page 556 ---
age  inconsistencies  and  consensual  association,  and
medical  records  having  shown  no  signs  of  forceful
intercourse.
4. Learned Counsel appearing for the State strongly opposed
the grant of suspension of sentence, highlighting the
matching FSL/DNA profile and the gravity of offences
involving a minor under the POCSO Act.
5. Having heard learned counsel for both parties and having
perused the material on record, without expressing any
final opinion on the merits of the appeal, we are of the
considered view that a prima facie case for suspension of
sentence is made out, given the custody period undergone,
absence of prior antecedents, and the arguable legal
issues raised regarding the age determination of the
victim.
6. Accordingly, the execution of the substantive sentence of
imprisonment awarded to the petitioners (Ashish Kumar @
Monu and Naveen Kumar @ Lala) in FIR No. 45/2024, P.S.
Bissau, District Jhunjhunu, shall remain suspended during
the pendency of the appeal before the High Court. 
7. The Trial Court shall release the petitioners on bail on
such conditions as deemed fit and appropriate, on the
basis of the suspension of sentence granted by us pending
appeal.  In  the  event  of  breach  of  any  conditions
specified above, it shall be open to the State to move an
SLP(Crl.)  No.12819/2026                                             3

--- Page 557 ---

O R D E R 
1. Leave granted.
2. Heard  learned  counsel  for  the
parties.
3. This  appeal  arises  from  an  order
dated 16.04.2026 passed by the High Court of
Judicature  at  Allahabad  rejecting  the
regular bail prayer of the appellant in
connection with Case Crime No. 277/2022,
registered at P.S. Gauri Bazar, District
Deoria. 
4. At the outset, learned counsel for
the appellant submits that he has suffered
pending trial incarceration of over four
1

--- Page 567 ---
years. Besides, it is a strange case where
prosecutrix  version,  though  learnt  on
22.02.2022, was reported to the police for
the fist time on 15.07.2022. It has been
submitted  that  the  appellant  has  been
falsely implicated.
5. The learned Counsel for the State-
respondent has opposed the prayer for bail
by  submitting  that  it  would  not  be
appropriate for us to make any observation
on the merits of the case as the trial is at
an  advance  stage.  However,  the  learned
counsel could not deny that the appellant
has suffered pending trial incarceration of
over four years.
6. Having regard to the fact that the
appellant  has  suffered  pending  trial
incarceration of over four years and there
appears some delay in lodging the First
Information Report, without expressing any
opinion on the merits of the case, we are of
the view that the appellant is entitled to
be released on bail at this stage.
2

--- Page 568 ---
7. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The order passed by the High Court rejecting
the regular bail prayer of the appellant is
set aside.
8. The appellant shall be released on
bail on such terms and conditions as the
trial court may deem fit to impose in the
facts and circumstances of the case.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall
stand disposed of.

CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.        OF 2026
(ARISING OUT OF S.L.P. (C) NO.29147 OF 2025)
THE STATE OF JHARKHAND & ORS.  ...APPELLANTS
VERSUS
ASHIANA HOUSING LIMITED & ANR.     ...RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The issue for consideration before us arises out of
the impugned order dated 18.12.2024 of the High Court of
Jharkhand by which, the application preferred by the
appellant for condonation of delay of 306 days in filing
the appeal before the High Court, has been rejected and
the  Letters  Patent  Appeal  has  been  dismissed
consequently. 
3. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the
appellants and the learned Senior counsel appearing for
the respondents at length.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants
submits that the period of delay is only of 240 days
1

--- Page 579 ---
which has been wrongly recorded by the High Court as 306
days in filing the appeal.
5. The  learned  Senior  counsel  appearing  for  the
respondents submits that much water has flown under the
bridge pursuant to the earlier order passed by the
learned Single Judge of the High Court.  The dispute is
pending  for  more  than  a  decade  and  deserves  no
interference of this Court.
6. Suffice it is to reiterate that we are only concerned
with the issue of condonation of delay.  The delay is not
found to be huge.  We find that the contentious issues
involved in the appeal which has been dismissed at the
threshold  on  the  question  of  delay,  deserve
consideration.
7. In such view of the matter, keeping all the issues
open including the contention as against the similar
orders passed in appeals preferred by the appellants, the
impugned order of the High Court is set aside and the
delay in filing the appeal before the High Court is
condoned.  Accordingly, the Letters Patent Appeal in LPA
No.394/2024 is restored on the file of the High Court and
the High Court shall decide the matter on merits.
8. Accordingly, the Civil Appeal is allowed.
2

--- Page 580 ---
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Application for exemption from filing certified copy of the
impugned judgment is allowed.
1

--- Page 600 ---
2. Learned senior counsel drawing attention to the prayer clause
in the Writ Petition submits that the individual respondents who
were the writ petitioners before the High Court herein had not even
challenged the validity of the Himachal Pradesh Panchayati Raj
(Amendment) Act, 2025 and, more particularly, Section 20 of the
amending Act which in turn amended Section 120 of the principal Act
and inserted sub-Section (4).  After the amendment, Section 120(4)
reads as under:
“(4) If a Panchayat is not constituted due to force-
majeure conditions or boycott by general public or due
to some other reasons after the issue of election
programme by the State Election Commission, the term of
such  Panchayat  constituted  later  on  shall  run
concurrently with other Panchayats of the State.”
3. Learned  senior  counsel  submits  that  two  of  the  writ
petitioners had even lost the election. Learned senior counsel
submits that till date, the petitioners are in-charge and the whole
purpose of the amendment was to bring uniformity in the conduct of
elections and the tenure of Panchayats constituted pursuant to the
elections.  Learned senior counsel submits that the amendment
enables the State to hold elections in one go.
4. Learned senior counsel further contends that the High Court by
staying the operation of the Notification dated 24 th June, 2026 has
rendered Section 120(4), as amended, nugatory and otiose.
5. Issue notice, returnable on 10th August, 2026.
2

--- Page 601 ---
6. Liberty is granted to serve dasti, in addition.
7. Till the next date of hearing, there shall be interim stay of
operation of the impugned order.

1. The Writ Petition was filed by the secured creditor, the
respondent herein. The respondent was before the High Court since
the order passed by the Debts Recovery Tribunal, Pune, was not
complied with by the petitioners herein and they were alleged to be
squatting on the property in which the respondent had a security
interest. The High Court permitted the borrowers to settle the loan
account with the secured creditor as ordered by the Debts Recovery
Tribunal, Pune, failing which the revenue authorities were directed
to take physical possession with police protection, for the purpose
of handing it over to the secured creditor.
2. This Court by order dated 29.05.2026 raised specific queries
as to the total dues payable and the one time settlement possible,
to have a quietus to the matter. On the submission of the
authorized officer of the respondent-company who was present in
person, an OTS was offered for Rs.1,80,00,000/- (Rupees One crore
and eighty lakh). It was directed that Rs.65,00,000/- (Rupees Sixty
five lakh) would be deposited on or before 15.07.2026 without fail.
The same has been deposited.
3. Today the petitioner No.1 has filed an undertaking agreeing to
pay the balance as per the following schedule:-
S.No. Tranche Amount Due Due Date
First Installment Rs. 30,00,000/- 31.08.2026
Second Installment Rs. 30,00,000/- 30.09.2026
Third Installment Rs. 30,00,000/- 31.10.2026
Fourth Installment Rs. 25,00,000/- 30.11.2026
Total Rs. 1,15,00,000/-
4. On the above amounts being paid, we direct the 1 st respondent
herein to hand over possession of the subject property to the

--- Page 616 ---
petitioners herein. It is also made clear that if one installment
is defaulted, then 1st respondent would be entitled to proceed
against the property.
5. On settlement of the entire amount, we further direct that all
proceedings i.e., civil and criminal, between the petitioners and
the 1st respondent shall stand closed. The 1st respondent shall
withdraw whatever proceedings are initiated against the petitioners
herein and the petitioners shall also do so if any proceedings are
initiated against the respondents.
6. Insofar as the FIR registered and the complaint proceeded
with, the 1st respondent shall co-operate and facilitate the
closure of such complaints or investigation without any further
prejudice to the petitioners.
7. We make it once again clear that the directions by us to hand
over possession of the property, encumbrance free and along with
the security documents deposited before the 1st respondent and the

as per the undertaking before this Court.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION 
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.             OF 2026
[Arising from SLP (Crl.) NO.            of 2026]
(Diary No(s). 43319/2026)
RAVI SRICHAND PUNJABI           APPELLANT(S)      
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MAHARASHTRA RESPONDENT(S)     
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Leave granted.
3. The present appeal is filed against the order
dated 16.04.2026 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Bombay passed in Interim Application No.1101 of 2026 in
Interim Application No.3806 of 2025 in Criminal Appeal
No.216  of  2025,  whereby  the  High  Court  rejected  the
application of the appellant seeking withdrawal of the
security amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs Only)
deposited by him.
4. The  appellant,  pursuant  to  the  order  dated
18.12.2025 passed by this Court, had deposited a sum of
Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs only) as security to
enable him to travel abroad. The appellant has since
returned India after his visit abroad.
5. Thereafter, the appellant applied before the High
Court for refund of the security amount of Rs.10,00,000/-
1

--- Page 639 ---
(Rupees Ten Lakhs only). The High Court, however, rejected
the  application  on  the  ground  that  since  the  order
directing deposit of the security amount had been passed by
this Court, the appellant ought to approach this Court for
refund of the said amount. 
6. Admittedly, the security amount was required to
be deposited only to ensure the appellant’s return to India
after  his  travel  abroad.  Now,  as  the  appellant  has
returned, he is entitled to refund of the said amount. 
7. Accordingly,  the  amount  of  Rs.10,00,000/-
(Rupees Ten Lakhs only) lying deposited with the High Court
of Judicature Bombay as security shall be refunded to the
appellant, along with accrued interest, if any, within two
weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of
this order.
8. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 16.04.2026
is set aside and the appeal is allowed.
9. Pending applications also stand disposed of.
....................,J.
       (VIKRAM NATH)
....................,J.
   (SANDEEP MEHTA)

Jaipur, Rajasthan.
4. We are conscious of the fact that whenever proceedings are

1

--- Page 654 ---
the other. More particularly, the Investigating Officer. In
such circumstances, as far as possible, Trial Court should not
insist for the physical presence of the Investigating Officer,
when his turn comes to lead oral evidence. His evidence can be
recorded online.

                             O R D E R
1. The present Special Leave Petition arises out of the impugned
judgment and order dated 19.05.2026 passed by the High Court of
Judicature  for  Rajasthan,  Bench  at  Jaipur,  in  S.B.  Criminal
Miscellaneous Bail Application No.5304/2026.
2. This Court, vide order dated 03.07.2026, granted interim bail
to the petitioner up to 14.07.2026 on the ground that he wants to
attend the surgery of his father scheduled to take place on
07.07.2026. However, as the matter was not heard finally, the
interim order dated 03.07.2026 was extended till the next date of
hearing.
3. Mr. Maninder Singh, learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf
of the petitioner, raised various grounds in the bail petition and
placed reliance upon the judgments/orders in Ratnambar Kaushik Vs.
Union of India, (2023) 2 SCC 621 ; Vineet Jain Vs. Union of India,
2025 SCC OnLine SC 2331; Ashutosh Garg Vs. Union of India, 2024 SCC
OnLine SC 5804; Krishan Damani Vs. State of West Bengal, (SLP
(Crl.) No.6954/2024); Abdulmajid Abdulsattar Memon Vs. State of
Gujarat; and Sanjay Jain Vs. Union of India . This Court has
carefully gone through the aforesaid judgments/orders.
4. Mr.  Raghvendra  P.  Shankar,  learned  Additional  Solicitor
General,  has  vehemently  argued  before  this  Court  that  the
petitioner is having two more cases and one of a similar nature and
has caused huge loss to the State exchequer. He is a habitual
offender. He has also stated that the petitioner is not entitled to
PETITION(S) FOR SPECIAL LEAVE TO APPEAL (CRL.)  NO(S).  10719/2026

--- Page 712 ---
3
grant of bail. He has further stated that the matter is fixed for
framing of charges; however, there is no Special Judge posted at
the relevant place, and therefore, the charges are not being
framed.
5. This Court, keeping in view the criminal antecedents of the
petitioner, is of the opinion that, at present, the petitioner is
not entitled to grant of bail. So far as framing of charges is
concerned, Hon’ble the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court is
requested to post a Special Judge as soon as possible so that the
trial is expedited and framing of charges takes place. At this
stage, this Court does not find any reason to allow the bail
petition. The petitioner, who is on interim bail, is granted two
weeks’ time to surrender before the concerned Court.

                             O R D E R
1. We heard Mr. Amit Sibal, the learned Senior counsel
appearing for the petitioners (original plaintiffs) and Mr.
Shreeyash U. Lalit, the learned counsel appearing for the
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 respectively (original Defendant Nos.3

--- Page 714 ---
2
and 4) 
2. The High Court while allowing the revision application
preferred by the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 respectively  and
thereby rejecting the plaint, has observed in para 49 of its
impugned Judgment and Order as follows:-
“In law, once a decree is passed on the basis of a compromise
between parties before the court, any person who was not a
party to that proceeding,, cannot assail the decree by way of a
separate suit. The only remedies available in such circumstances
are either to prefer an appeal under Section 96(1) of the Code
of Civil Procedure with the leave of the Appellate Court, or to
move a review application before the very court which passed
the decree.”
3. We are of the view that insofar as the decision of the
High Court to reject the plaint on the premise that the suit
is not maintainable is concerned, no error not to speak of any
error of law, could be said to have been committed by the High
Court in taking such view. High Court has made itself very
clear that the only remedy available to the petitioners before
us was to prefer an appeal under Section 96(1) of the Civil
Procedure Code with the leave of the Appellate Court or to
move a review petition before the very Court which passed the
decree. 
4. With the liberty to avail appropriate remedies as noted
by the High Court in para 49 of the impugned Judgment and
Order and subject to the law of limitation, we leave it open
to the petitioners to avail appropriate legal remedies before
the appropriate forum in accordance with law. 
5. It is needless to clarify that if the petitioners deem
fit to seek leave to appeal before the Appellate Court or
prefer a Review Petition before the very court which passed
the decree, the same shall be decided on its own merits in
accordance with law.

--- Page 715 ---
3
6. With the aforesaid, this petition stands disposed of.
7. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

further claims of the appellant (landlord), more particularly the

forward before the competent Authority in accordance with law.

reporting compliance of our directions as regards removal of the
plant and machinery, referred to above.
6. Unfortunately, the CoC has failed to remove the machinery
despite the fact that it had undertaken before us that they would
do so.
7. CoC has many grounds to urge as to why they have not been able
to remove the machinery, more particularly, the ground that the
cost they are likely to incur for the removal is almost about
Rs.7 Crore. 
8. Be that as it may, it is high time that we put aside the CoC.

Interlocutory Application No. 271514/2025 in Criminal
Appeal No.4809/2025
1. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant as
well as learned counsel for the respondent-State of
West Bengal.
1

--- Page 729 ---
2. This Interlocutory Application has been filed by
the  appellant  for  enlarging  him  on  bail  pending
consideration of the Criminal Appeal.
3. It may be mentioned that appellant was convicted
by the Trial Court under Sections 120B, 396, 201 and
412 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, ‘IPC’)
and sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that co-
convict has been granted bail by this Court vide order
dated 28.07.2026. Therefore, similar privilege may be
extended to the present appellant.
5. On  the  other  hand,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State  of  West  Bengal  submits  that  the
offence for which appellant has been convicted is a
heinous one which has been proved in trial. Therefore,
appellant may not be enlarged on bail.
6. Submissions  made  by  learned  counsel  for  the
parties have been duly considered.
7. We find that like the case of the co-convict in
Interlocutory  Application  No.282648/2025  in  Special
Leave Petition (Criminal) No.15787/2025, who has been
granted bail, appellant herein has also undergone more
than 16 years of incarceration.
8. In the circumstances, we are of the view that a
case for bail is made out.
9. Accordingly, we direct that pending consideration
of Criminal Appeal No.4809/2025, appellant shall be
2

--- Page 730 ---
enlarged  on  bail.  For  this  purpose,  he  shall  be
produced before the Trial Court within a maximum period
of  07  days  from  today,  whereafter  he  shall  be
released on bail on such terms and conditions as may
be deemed appropriate.
10. Interlocutory  Application  No.271514/2025  is
disposed of.
11. List the Criminal Appeal in due course.

(@SLP(CRL.) NO.11606 OF 2026)
RAJESH LAKANDRI & ORS. ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF ASSAM ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant(s) and Mr. Debojit
Borkakati, learned AOR, appearing on advance notice for the respondent-
State extensively.
2. Since  no  order  adverse  to  the  interest  of  the  respondent  is  passed,
question of granting any further time to the respondent does not arise.
Permitted to file vakalatnama within two weeks from today.
3. Leave granted.
4. This appeal is directed against the order dated 18.02.2026 whereunder
the jurisdictional High Court, while  considering the appeal alongwith the
application filed under Section 430 of BNSS for suspension of sentence and
grant of bail, has ordered the appeal to be listed for final hearing in the first
week of May, 2026, without adjudicating the application for suspension of
sentence.
5. Though we do not find any fault with the impugned order, however, we
cannot be oblivious to the fact that appellant(s) has a right to seek for
1

--- Page 765 ---
suspension of sentence in a pending criminal appeal. As such, we request
the High Court to consider the application which is filed for suspension of
sentence in the event of appeal not being taken up on the next date of
hearing for final disposal.
6. However, we make it clear that in the event of appeal itself being taken
up for final hearing, question of considering the application for suspension of
sentence, may not arise. We leave it to the discretion of the jurisdictional
High Court to regulate its proceedings as it may choose to do so.
7. With this observation, the appeal stands disposed of.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned
counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Appellant has been convicted in FIR No.02/2006, registered at
Police Station Patwari Circle Mangroli, Sub-Division: Karanprayag,
District- Chamoli, Uttarakhand, under Section 363 of the Indian
1

--- Page 768 ---
Penal Code, 1860 (for short, ‘IPC’) and sentenced to undergo
Rigorous Imprisonment (RI) for 4 years and fine with a default
stipulation.
4. Appeal filed by the appellant before the High Court was
dismissed.
5. This Court by Order dated 06.02.2026, had issued notice
whereafter State has filed counter affidavit.
6. We find in this case that the victim could not be examined in
court as she committed suicide before the trial could commence.
Therefore, prima-facie there appears to be no evidence to connect
the appellant with the offence. Though, learned counsel for the
State would submit that PW-9, the hotel manager, had deposed that
both the appellant and the victim had stayed in the hotel on
03.02.2006 and had checked out of the hotel in the morning of
04.02.2006, there is nothing on record to show that the appellant
had abducted the victim. The victim did not even raise any
objection or hue and cry at the hotel.
7. In the circumstances, we are of the view that a case for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail is made out.
8. We, however, make it clear that our observations made above
are tentative, only for the purpose of considering suspension of
sentence and grant of bail.
9. Accordingly, we direct that the appellant shall be produced
before the concerned Sessions Judge within a maximum period of 7
days from today, whereafter the learned Sessions Judge shall
release the petitioner on bail on such terms and conditions as may
be deemed appropriate.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
   CIVIL APPEAL NO.3513 OF 2024
    
SURESH CHANDRA BHATT                                  APPELLANT
                                                            VERSUS
SATISH SINGH FARTYAL & ANR.             RESPONDENTS
O R D E R
1. The present appeal has been filed by the appellant-advocate challenging the
judgment dated 30.08.2019 passed by the Uttarakhand High Court in Second Appeal
No.106 of 2019 whereby, the Second Appeal filed by the respondent no.2 herein was
dismissed and cost of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) each was imposed on the
respondent no.2 and the appellant.  It is pertinent to mention that the Appellant was
the counsel representing respondent no.2.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant-advocate states that the respondent no.2 had
engaged the appellant for filing of First Appeal before the High Court against the
decree of divorce without disclosing to him that the First Appeal filed before the
District Court had been dismissed. 
3. He contended that this Court in Neeraj Garg v. Sarita Rani & Ors.  (2021) 9
SCC 92 and  Siddhartha Singh v. Assistant Collector First Class/Sub Divisional
Magistrate  C.A.Nos.11043-11044  of  2024  has  observed  with  disapproval  the

--- Page 798 ---
2
proclivity of the same learned Judge of the High Court in making remarks against the
counsel.
4. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the view that
the cost of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) imposed on the appellant as counsel
for respondent no.2 and adverse remarks against the counsel are liable to be set aside
as the said order has been passed without affording him an opportunity of hearing.
5. Consequently, the impugned judgment being in violation of principles of natural
justice  is  set  aside  to  the  extent  it  imposes  cost  of  Rs.50,000/-  (Rupees  Fifty
Thousand) on the appellant-advocate. The observations/findings against the conduct
of appellant-advocate in paragraph no.2 of the impugned judgment are also set aside.
6. With the aforesaid direction, the Civil Appeal is disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
          …………………J.
[MANMOHAN] 
…………………J.
                            [N.V.ANJARIA]
NEW DELHI
JULY 30, 2026

Court of Illaka/duty Magistrate, Gurugram to a Court of competent  
jurisdiction at Samastipur, Bihar.  Be it stated that the domestic  
violence case has been instituted by the mother-in-law seeking  
prohibitory orders against the petitioner-wife (daughter-in-law).
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that parties are  
from  Samastipur  Bihar,  though  the  husband  by  virtue  of  his  
avocation, is residing at Gurugram. He submits that petitioner-wife  
has instituted two proceedings at Samastipur, one pertaining to  
maintenance  and  the  other  under  the  Domestic  Violence  Act.

Samastipur.

is made out.

jurisdiction at Samastipur, Bihar.
8.  It would be open to the respondent-husband to move the Court of  
competent jurisdiction at Samastipur, Bihar to appear through  
virtual mode, if the occasion so arises.

I.A. No. 91640/2026
1.  We have heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing
for the parties and perused the counter affidavit filed
on behalf of respondent No.23, the official respondent
(EPFO).
2.  In the said counter affidavit, a specific reference
has been made to paragraph 38, which reads thus:
“38. In view of the facts and circumstances
stated above, it is respectfully prayed that
this Hon’ble Court may be pleased to dispose
the present Special Leave Petition.  It is
further prayed that the answering respondents
be permitted to allow the promotions to the
post of Enforcement Officer / Accounts Officer
(EO/AO), subject to the final decision/outcome
of the present case by this Hon’ble Court.”
3.  Suffice it is to observe that this Interlocutory
Application deserves to be allowed without prejudice to
the contentions made in the Special Leave Petition, as
withholding the promotion shall not benefit any of the
parties involved and is also contrary to public interest.
4. In view of the above, we allow the Interlocutory
Application subject to outcome of the final order to be
passed in the Special Leave Petition. Accordingly,  the
Interlocutory Application stands allowed.
5. Promotion order to be passed in pursuance of this
order, will not give any right to the other parties.

1. The petitioner has been denied anticipatory bail by the High
Court in connection with GD Entry No. 46 dated 12.11.2024 in FIR
No. 301 of 2024 dated 12.11.2024 registered with PS Phillaur,
District Jalandhar Rural, Punjab for the offence punishable under
Sections 118(2), 115(2), 74, 191(3), and 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita (for short "the BNS").
2. The prosecution case arises out of an alleged clash between
two groups, which resulted in physical altercation. The complainant
alleges that the petitioner struck him on the head with a sharp-

--- Page 1030 ---
edged rod, causing a deep incised wound on his skull, which is
grievous in nature. GD Entry No. 46 is a cross-complaint against
the abovementioned FIR, which was filed by a relative of the
petitioner.
3. The order impugned herein was challenged by the counsel for
the petitioner on various grounds, such as the chargesheet not yet
having been filed, that the petitioner was not arrested for more
than 1 year and 6 months, absence of recovery, as well as the grant
of anticipatory bail to some of the accused persons in FIR 301 of
2024. It was also submitted by the counsel that the petitioner is
an employee with the Fire and Rescue Services in the State of
Punjab.
4. We order that in the event of arrest of the petitioner in
connection  with  the  offence  enumerated  above,  they  shall  be
released on bail, subject to the terms and conditions that the I.O.
may deem fit to impose, on condition also of continued cooperation
in the investigation.
5. Once the petitioner is released on bail by the I.O., on
directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the Sessions
Judge, Jalandhar (the jurisdictional court), the petitioner shall
appear before the jurisdictional court and furnish fresh bail bonds
and ensure due appearance in the trial.
6. With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.

3. Respondent-State of Rajasthan may file its counter affidavit within one

the petitioner(s) to withdraw the Special Leave Petition by granting liberty as

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. For alleged violation of the order dated 19.01.2023 passed in LPA 425 of
2022, contempt proceedings have been initiated. The said order passed in the
LPA, is an offshoot of the challenge laid to a common order dated 04.08.2022
passed in WP(L) No.2535 of 2021, whereby a challenge was laid to the award
dated 04.07.2014 passed in Reference No.47 of 2007, under which the Central
Government  Industrial  Tribunal  (CGIT)  directed  the  petitioner  herein  not  to
remove  the  workers  and  to  regularize  the  110  workers  working  in  BSNL,
Daltonganj, Ranchi, 20-25 persons annually within a period of five years and the
said award came to be published on 17.02.2015.
2. For execution of the said award, there is already an execution petition filed in
Execution Case No.11/2001. On acco unt of pendency of the parent SLP, the
execution proceedings is said to have not been taken up. Hence, reserving
liberty  to the  said Executing Court to proceed in accordance  with law, the
present Special Leave Petitions are disposed of with following observation.
3.  We are making it explicitly clear that workmen, either by themselves or
through Union, cannot ride two boats at a time and the contempt proceedings
initiated in Contempt Petition No.925 of 2025  would not survive in view of the
execution proceedings already having been taken. Hence, reserving liberty to
the  workmen  to  proceed  with  the  execution  proceedings,  the  contempt
proceedings stands set aside or dropped. The execution proceedings shall be
expeditiously disposed of on merits.
4. Accordingly, the present Special Leave Petitions stand disposed of.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard the learned Senior counsel appearing for the petitioner
– Assessee.
2. While answering the substantial question of law in favour of
the Revenue, the High Court took the view that capital profit on
the sale of the fixed assets of the Company cannot be taken
directly to the reserves and surplus in the balance sheet and the
same has to be routed through the profit and loss account to arrive
at the correct book profits under Section 115 JB of the Income Tax
Act, 1961.
3. Exemption Application is allowed.
4. Issue notice, returnable in four weeks.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The submission on behalf of the appellant is that
the issue whether income from sale of seeds after
processing the same would amount to agricultural income
or business income, arises for our consideration. It
has been submitted that the High Court in its impugned
1

--- Page 1472 ---
order has placed reliance on the decision of the Income
Tax Appellate Tribunal in the case of Indo American
Exports and Namdhari Seeds (P) Ltd. dated 14.07.2006.
It is submitted that the said decision of ITAT was
subject to an Income Tax Appeal before the Karnataka
High Court and was set aside by the Division Bench of
the Karnataka High Court vide order dated 24.10.2011.
It  has also  been submitted  that the  civil appeal
against the said order is pending in this Court as
Civil Appeal No.356 of 2015.
2. The learned counsel for the assessee/respondent
submits that the case of Namdhari on which reliance has
been placed is distinguishable on facts because here
the land over which the seeds were cultivated were
leased  out  by  the  assessee  company.  It  is  also
submitted that the farmers are cultivating the land on
behalf of the assessee company and, therefore, the
assessee company itself can qualify as a cultivator.
3. All the aforesaid aspects can be better examined
after the receipt of response.
4. Delay condoned.
5. Issue notice, returnable in six weeks.
6. Notice on behalf of respondent has been accepted
by Mr. E. C. Agrawala, Advocate.

Service  was  complete  on  respondent  nos.  1  and  2  in
February/March, 2026   but none has entered appearance.
As per office report, ld. Counsel for the petitioner had
filed an application seeking substituted service on respondent
no.3 by way of publication in newspapers, ‘Rajasthan Patrika’,
Hindi language and ‘Prompt Times’, English language which was
allowed  vide  order  dt.27.04.2026.  Now  ld.  Counsel  for  the
petitioner has filed an affidavit of publication stating therein
Contd….

--- Page 1526 ---
-2-
Item no.21
that instead of publishing the notice in ‘Rajasthan Patrika',
petitioner has published the notice in 'Udaipur Express'(Hindi
edition), as publication in ‘Rajasthan Patrika’ was found to
involve  disproportionately  high  charges.  Ld.  Counsel  has
submitted that ‘Udaipur Express' is a widely circulated Hindi
daily in the concerned area and “The Prompt” is the only English
newspaper published in the concerned area,  however it is a
weekly newspaper & no English daily newspaper is  published
there.  Publication  in  an  English  daily  newspaper  published
outside Udaipur would involve  disproportionately high charges.
Therefore, while the petitioner contends that the publication in
‘Udaipur Express’ sufficiently serves the purpose of substituted
service, but by way of abundant caution seeks leave of the
Hon’ble Court to publish the notice in ‘The Prompt’, English
newspaper.
List the matter before Hon’ble Judge in Chambers seeking
necessary directions.

concerned ld. Advocate-on-record for information and compliance.
